_about: The hope hub (plan 7.6f), built the way love and righteousness are: the rows are defined by the Hebrew and Greek, a noun row by the words standing in the noun's own phrase or verse, a verb row by the verb's frame or the verse, and a verse sits in every row it fits (match: all). The review panel flagged hope medium (committee-flags.json): 'the hope of Israel' and 'the hope of the gospel' will be read as one hope or two, and pooling the Hebrew words with ἐλπίς overstates equivalence. So: each phrase is its own row, as written, side by side, with a note that the page takes no side; the Hebrew and the Greek are kept in rows of their own wherever the companion words differ (the LORD / God, below); no row says whose hope it is. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/hope.json.

titles.noun: What the text says of hope

_forms_why: h6960 קָוָה has no lexicon entry, so the builder would type it a noun and its verb verses would stand in the noun rows

sense_keep.Isa.42.4: Berean: 'In His law the islands will put their hope' (MACULA glosses יָחַל 'wait')
sense_keep.Isa.51.5: Berean: 'The islands will look for Me and wait in hope for My arm' (both verbs glossed 'wait')
sense_keep.Job.6.11: Berean: 'What strength do I have, that I should still hope?' (יָחַל glossed 'wait')
sense_keep.Ps.31.24: Berean: 'all you who hope in the LORD' (יָחַל glossed 'wait')
sense_keep.Isa.49.23: Berean: 'those who hope in Me will never be put to shame' (קָוָה glossed 'wait for')
sense_keep.Ps.37.9: Berean: 'those who hope in the LORD will inherit the land' (קָוָה glossed 'wait for')
sense_keep.Ps.69.6: Berean: 'May those who hope in You not be ashamed through me' (קָוָה glossed 'wait for')

_words_why: The card's own words: ἐλπίς and ἐλπίζω; the Hebrew nouns תִּקְוָה, מִקְוֶה, תּוֹחֶלֶת, מַבָּט, שֵׂבֶר; and the two Hebrew verbs the English renders 'hope' in part, יָחַל and קָוָה. Both are mostly 'wait' (יָחַל 'wait' in 23 of its 42 verses, קָוָה in 32 of its 45), so they count ONLY where the verse renders them hope or expect (the 'sense' below): 'Wait for the LORD' (Ps 27:14) is waiting and is not here, 'put your hope in the LORD' (Ps 130:7) is. Where MACULA glosses 'wait' but the Berean itself prints 'hope' (Isa 42:4, 51:5, 49:23; Job 6:11; Ps 31:24, 37:9, 69:6), 'sense_keep' keeps the verse with its reason; the original (the same verb) is the one in all of them. The same sense rule drops תִּקְוָה 'cord' (Josh 2:18, 2:21) and מִקְוֶה 'reservoirs, gathering' (Gen 1:10, Exod 7:19, Lev 11:36). The Hebrew and Greek words are not pooled as one: every example names the word it stands on, and the rows below that differ by language (the LORD, God) are separate.
_sense_why: 'hop' is hope, hoped, hoping; 'expect' is the Hebrew 'expectation' (Prov 10:28, 11:23) and the Greek 'you expect' (Luke 6:34); 'relied on' is the one place (Isa 20:6, מַבָּט) where MACULA's gloss says 'relied on' and the Berean reads 'our source of hope', beside Isa 20:5 where the same word is 'hope'.

Ps.34.1.why: the builder files MACULA's Ps 33:22 under Ps 34:1 (the Berean prints the heading and 34:1 together); the word is at 33:22: 'as we put our hope in You'

Isa.64.2.why: MACULA's Isa 64:2 is the Berean's 64:3 ('awesome works that we did not expect'); the Berean's 64:2 has no such word

others._why: Words the English renders 'hope' that are not this concept's own words (as love names φιλέω and חֶסֶד apart). The rows stand on ἐλπίς, תִּקְוָה and the rest above; a different word the English also calls 'hope' is named apart with its verses and never handed over as the same.
others.title: Other words translated “hope”

_review: Not yet reviewed. The panel's flag (medium): keep 'the hope of Israel', 'the hope of glory', 'the hope of the resurrection' each as written and in its own row; mark Hebrew and Greek separately; leave out any row that implies who the hope belongs to. Taken so: those three are three rows, and 'the hope of the gospel, the calling, righteousness, salvation, eternal life' a fourth; no row is by whose hope it is; the rows about the LORD and God are by hand, in a Hebrew row and a Greek row; the verb rows are by what is said and where the hope is set, not by who the subject is (Paul, Herod, 'the nations' stand in the rows their verses fit).

rows.label: Hope with faith and love
rows._why: merged from 'Hope and faith' (10) and 'Hope and love' (5): one row, a verse that names both stands once

rows.label: The Holy Spirit named with hope
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: the three verses that name the Spirit beside hope. How the text relates them (power, the one through whom, the giver) is in the verses and the page does not choose

rows.label: Christ named with hope
rows.note: The verses where the text itself names Christ beside hope. How it relates them -- Christ as the hope, its ground, the one in whom it is set -- is in the verses, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: by hand: a rule on Christ/κύριος would take every 'Lord' (Ps 71:5, 'Lord GOD') and decide a person the text has not named

rows.label: The LORD, God and hope
rows._why: Hebrew, by hand: the verses where the text names the LORD or God beside the Hebrew noun ('You are my hope, O Lord GOD'; 'the LORD, the hope of their fathers'). Jer 14:8 ('O Hope of Israel, its Savior') added on Doug's decision, 2026-10-10: the prayer names the LORD at 14:7 and 14:9, either side of it; it stays under Israel as well

rows.label: God and hope
rows._why: Greek, by hand, apart from the Hebrew row above: the verses where the text names God beside ἐλπίς ('the God of hope'; 'hope in God'). 1 Thess 1:3, where 'our God and Father' stands near a hope 'in our Lord Jesus Christ', is left to the Christ row

rows.label: Hope and Israel

not_verses.Eph.2.12: 'alienated from the commonwealth of Israel ... without hope' says the Gentiles had no hope, not that the hope is Israel's

rows.note: Jer 14:8 and 17:13 call the LORD the hope of Israel (Hebrew מִקְוֶה); Acts 28:20 and 26:7 are Paul's Greek (ἐλπίς); Ezra 10:2 and Ezek 37:11 use תִּקְוָה. These are different words, set side by side as written; the page does not say whether they are one hope. Whether the hope of Israel and the hope of the gospel are one or two, the page takes no side.
rows._add_why: Acts 26:7: 'the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled' -- Israel named as the twelve tribes, which the rule (the word Israel) does not read
rows._lead_why: Ezra 10:2 stays in the row but not among the first four shown: read cold it opens the dismissal of foreign wives, and a hope hub should not lead with that (panel); Ezek 37:11 shows both words

rows.label: The hope of glory
rows.note: The text's phrases, kept as written: 'the hope of glory' (Col 1:27), 'the hope of the glory of God' (Rom 5:2).

rows.label: The hope of the gospel, the calling, righteousness, salvation, eternal life; hope and being saved, the Savior
rows.note: Each phrase kept as written. Where readers part on whose hope it is -- the church's, Israel's, or both -- or on what 'the hope of righteousness' (Gal 5:5) is, the page takes no side.
rows._why: merged from the gospel row (7) and 'Hope and salvation, the Savior' (6). The 'hope of ...' phrases are the rule; the Greek verses that name being saved or the Savior beside hope (1 Tim 1:1, Rom 8:24, Titus 2:13) are added by hand. Panel fix 2026-10-10: Jer 14:8 (a Hebrew address to the LORD, מִקְוֶה, stays under 'Hope and Israel') and Acts 27:20 (sailors hoping to survive, stays under 'Hope lost') are out of this row

rows.label: Hope and the resurrection
rows.note: Acts 23:6 and 24:15 name the resurrection of the dead, 1 Pet 1:3 the resurrection of Jesus Christ; the page does not say which is meant to be the hope.

rows.label: Hope, the promise and the word

not_verses.1Pet.3.15: λόγος here is 'reason' (an account of the hope), not the word

rows.label: Hope with endurance, suffering, comfort, joy and peace
rows._why: merged from 'endurance, suffering, comfort' (7) and 'joy, gladness and peace' (5). שָׁלוֹם is not in the list: at Jer 29:11 the Berean reads it 'to prosper', so the verse would not show 'peace'

rows.label: Hope with confidence and boldness, held fast, and shame
rows.note: Rom 5:5, hope that does not put to shame; Isa 20:5, those who made Cush their hope are ashamed; Jer 17:13, those who abandon the LORD, the hope of Israel, are put to shame. Set side by side as written.
rows._why: merged from 'boldness, confidence, assurance, security' (7), 'Hold fast to hope' (3) and 'Hope and shame' (5)

rows.label: There is hope; hope and a future
rows._why: merged from 'There is hope' (7) and 'Hope and the future' (4); Prov 23:18 and 24:14 ('there is a future ... your hope will not be cut off') now fit by the future
rows.note: Jer 29:11 and 31:17 are the LORD's word to the exiles of Judah (see 29:1, 29:10) and to Israel; Proverbs speaks of the one who finds wisdom.

rows.label: The hope of the righteous, the wicked, the godless, the poor and needy
rows._why: merged from 'The hope of the righteous, the wicked, the godless' (6) and 'Hope for the poor, the needy, the oppressed' (2)
rows.note: Several of the Job verses (5:16, 8:13, 11:20) are spoken by Job's friends, of whom the LORD says at Job 42:7 that they have not spoken rightly of Him; Proverbs and the Psalms speak in their own voice.

rows.label: Hope lost, perished, uprooted, withered; without hope

not_verses.Job.11.20: אָבַד is 'escape will elude them'; the hope there is the next clause's 'last breath'
not_verses.Ps.9.18: denies the loss: 'nor the hope of the oppressed forever dashed' -- a promise to the poor, kept in 'The hope of the righteous, the wicked, the godless, the poor and needy'

rows._why: merged from 'Hope lost, perished' (11) and 'Without hope' (4, by hand: 'without hope' is the Greek μὴ ἔχω ἐλπίδα and the Hebrew אֶפֶס, אַיִן, no one lemma a rule could read)
rows.note: Most of these are what someone in distress says, not what the text concludes: the LORD answers the exiles' words in Ezek 37:12-14.
rows._lead_why: Ezek 37:11 ('our hope has perished') stays in the row but no longer opens it: its answer is in 37:12-14, and the note says so

rows.label: Every other use
rows._why: includes the ordinary sense, kept: hope of making money (Acts 16:19), the plowman's hope of a share (1 Cor 9:10, where the Berean reads 'expect'); formerly its own row of two

rows.label: Hope in the LORD, in God
rows._why: Hebrew, by hand: the verses where the text names the LORD or God as the one in whom the hope is put. Job 13:15 ('I will hope in Him') and Ps 71:14 name no one in their own verse and stand under 'Every other use'. Ps 31:24, 37:9, 69:6 and Isa 49:23 name the LORD ('those who hope in the LORD'; 'hope in You, O Lord GOD'; 'I am the LORD; those who hope in Me') and are frameless or by hand because the divine persons are. Isa 8:17, where the Berean reads 'wait ... trust', stays under 'Every other use'. Two former rows are inside it by their verses: 'O my soul, put your hope in God' (Ps 42:5, 42:11, 43:5) and 'Hope and the LORD's loving devotion' (Ps 33:18, 33:22, 147:11, 130:7 -- 'those whose hope is in His loving devotion')
rows.note: The Hebrew verbs yachal (יָחַל) and qavah (קָוָה) are also rendered "wait" in about forty-seven verses (for example Ps 27:14, Ps 25:3, Isa 40:31, Mic 7:7); those are not listed here, only where the verse renders them hope or expect.

rows.label: Set hope on God
rows._why: Greek, by hand, apart from the Hebrew row above

rows.label: Christ named with hope
rows.note: The verses where the text itself names Christ beside the verb; the page does not decide how the hope relates to him.
rows._why: by hand, as the noun row

rows.label: Hope in the word, the judgments

not_verses.Isa.42.4: מִשְׁפָּט here is the justice the servant establishes, not judgments hoped in
not_verses.Isa.59.9: מִשְׁפָּט here is the justice hoped for, not God's judgments
not_verses.Isa.59.11: מִשְׁפָּט here is the justice hoped for, not God's judgments
not_verses.Ps.119.81: the Berean reads 'I wait for Your word' (MACULA glosses יָחַל 'hope' here); the verse stays under 'Every other use' so its English does not stand under a label it does not show

rows.label: Hope and Israel
rows.note: Israel is called to hope in the LORD (Ps 130:7, 131:3); Ps 69:6 is a prayer to the God of Israel; Luke 24:21 and Acts 26:7 are the disciples' and Paul's words about Israel's hope. Whether the hope of Israel and the hope of the gospel are one or two, the page takes no side.
rows._why: split from the former 'Hope and Israel; the nations, the islands will put their hope' (panel 2026-10-10: two different matters under one note). Acts 26:7: 'our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled'

rows.label: The nations, the islands will put their hope
rows.note: Matthew 12:21 quotes Isaiah 42:4; Romans 15:12 quotes Isaiah 11:10, where the Hebrew word is "seek". Who the nations hope in is in the verses; the page takes no side.
rows._why: split from the Israel row. Isa 42:4 and 51:5 are held by 'sense_keep' (the Berean prints hope). Correction of the first report: Rom 15:12 quotes Isa 11:10 (Hebrew 'seek', not 'hope'), not Isa 42:4; the Greek ἐλπίζω is in the verse as the Berean prints it

rows.label: Hope for what is not yet seen
rows._why: split from the former two-in-one row (panel: the NT assurance of the unseen and the Hebrew hope disappointed should not read as question and answer). Rom 8:24 and Heb 11:1 have no frame in the data the verb rules read, so by hand. Rom 8:20 ('in hope', of creation) opens the same passage but is the noun ἐλπίς and stands under the noun 'Every other use'

rows.label: Hoped for one thing, and another came
rows.note: In Isa 5:4 it is the LORD who expected sweet grapes; the others are the people's words.
rows._why: mostly קָוָה: 'we hope for light, but there is darkness'; 'I hoped for good, evil came'; 'I expected sweet grapes, did it bring forth sour fruit?' (Isa 5:4; Isa 5:2, where the Berean reads 'waited', is left under 'Every other use') -- a pattern the verses share and no one lemma marks, so by hand. Job 30:26 also has יָחַל (glossed 'waited', not counted)

rows.label: Hoping to come, to see, to send, to speak; hoping you will understand
rows._why: the ordinary sense, kept (Paul, John's 'elder', and Herod at Luke 23:8, 'hoping to see Him perform a miracle'); merged from two rows, the second ('I hope you will understand', 2 Cor 1:13, 13:6, 5:11) added by hand

rows.label: Every other use
rows._why: includes 'Hope of repayment, a bribe' (Luke 6:34, Acts 24:26), formerly its own row of two
